title: Step 28 Bochner-Killing center bound verification
scope: Ansatz-free global Killing center bound; model-level verification in the diagonal H3 cohomogeneity-one setting.

general_theorem.name: Bochner center bound for Killing fields
hypotheses: (M^n, g) is a closed Riemannian manifold
Z is a Killing vector field on M
general_theorem.proof: Bochner: for Z Killing, ΔZ + Ric(Z) = 0, hence ∫|∇Z|^2 = ∫Ric(Z,Z) <= (Λ+δ)∫|Z|^2

fiber_application.setup: If Z is the central Killing field of a nilpotent isometric action
fiber_application.pointwise_lower: |∇Z|^2 >= |∇^F Z|^2 = (b^2/2)|Z|^2 for Heisenberg center bracket b
fiber_application.sign_consequence: For Λ>0 and δ<Λ: b^2 <= 2(Λ+δ) on average (weighted by |Z|^2)

general_theorem.almost_Killing_extension: Replace Z Killing by ||L_Z g|| <= tau; error is O(tau) in the integrated bound

CH2_check.note: b^2=1 > 2*(-3/2)=-3: the bound b^2<=2(Λ+δ) is vacuous for Λ<0, as expected

comparison_with_step27.step27_result: |d log b/dt|^2 >= (5/4)(b^2+4Λ) on the constraint surface C_Λ=0
comparison_with_step27.bochner_result: ⟨b^2⟩_{|Z|^2} <= 2(Λ+δ) for any Killing Z with ∇^F lower bound
comparison_with_step27.relation: The Bochner result is weaker pointwise (averaged vs pointwise) but vastly more general: it does not require the diagonal cohomogeneity-one H3 ansatz, works in every dimension, has no O'Neill/T/A dependence, and only requires Z to be Killing. The ODE result is stronger within its model because it gives pointwise monotonicity and thin-shell structure.
hierarchy: Level 0: Bochner Killing center bound (ansatz-free, dim-free, Killing required)
Level 1: O'Neill submersion + Bochner (fiber structure needed, pointwise for T=0)
Level 2: Diagonal H3 ODE system (model-specific, pointwise monotonicity)
comparison_with_step27.complementarity: Level 0 settles the twist question: twist cannot evade the bound. Level 2 gives the strongest model theorem (thin shells, no plateau). The gap is Level 0.5: almost-Killing for N-structures.

induction_architecture.description: For a nilpotent isometric collapse with step-k nilpotent fiber N: (1) Take the center Killing field Z_k. Bochner bounds <b_k^2> <= 2(Λ+δ). (2) Quotient by the central circle. The Kaluza-Klein/O'Neill relation gives Ric_B = Ric^H + (1/2)φ∘φ on the quotient, keeping two-sided control with constants degrading at most linearly in the step. (3) The quotient has step-(k-1) nilpotent fiber. (4) Repeat. After k steps, all brackets are bounded, and the fiber is virtually abelian at the ambient scale.
induction_architecture.per_step_constants: Λ_new = Λ + O(b_k^2) = Λ + O(Λ) ~ 2Λ per step; after k steps, O(2^k Λ)
induction_architecture.total_degradation: Acceptable for fixed nilpotency step (bounded by n-1)
induction_architecture.key_hypothesis: Each central quotient preserves enough structure for Bochner on the next level
induction_architecture.sign_asymmetry: For Λ < 0, Bochner kills ALL Killing fields: ∫|∇Z|^2 = ∫Ric(Z,Z) < 0 if Z≠0 and Ric < 0, contradiction. So negative Ricci has no Killing fields at all; negative-branch collapse is never by isometries of a closed manifold.
